sn12.57:1.2: “Bhikkhus, when one dwells contemplating gratification in things that can fetter, craving increases.
sn12.57:1.3: With craving as condition, clinging comes to be….
sn12.57:1.4: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.57:2.2: and from time to time a man would clear the area around the roots, from time to time provide it with good soil, from time to time water it.
sn12.57:2.3: Sustained by that care, nourished by it, that sapling would attain to growth, increase, and expansion.
sn12.57:2.4: So too, when one dwells contemplating gratification in things that can fetter, craving increases….
sn12.57:2.6: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.57:3.1: “When, bhikkhus, one dwells contemplating danger in things that can fetter, craving ceases.
sn12.57:3.2: With the cessation of craving comes cessation of clinging….
sn12.57:3.3: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.57:4.2: Then a man would come along bringing a shovel and a basket.
sn12.57:4.3: He would cut down the sapling at its foot … as in §55 … he would winnow the ashes in a strong wind or let them be carried away by the swift current of a river.
sn12.57:4.4: Thus that sapling would be cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated so that it is no more subject to future arising.
sn12.57:4.5: “So too, bhikkhus, when one dwells contemplating danger in things that can fetter, craving ceases….
sn12.57:4.7: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”
